props.title: Diary of a Mad Housewife

sections.content: Diary of a Mad Housewife stands as a searing indictment of upper-middle-class marriage in late 1960s Manhattan, arriving at a pivotal moment in feminist cinema. Director Frank Perry and screenwriter Eleanor Perry adapt Sue Kaufman's novel into a razor-sharp character study that predates similar domestic alienation films like An Unmarried Woman (1978) and Kramer vs. Kramer (1979). Carrie Snodgress delivers a breakthrough performance as Tina Balser, a woman suffocating under her narcissistic husband's demands and finding hollow solace in an affair with a manipulative writer.

movies.title: A Woman Under the Influence
movies.slug: Cassavetes' raw examination of a housewife's mental breakdown and her family's response

sections.content: The film's unflinching portrayal of emotional abuse and psychological manipulation feels startlingly modern, particularly in Richard Benjamin's portrayal of Jonathan Balser - a social-climbing husband whose constant belittlement of his wife masks his own deep insecurities. Like Revolutionary Road (2008) and Far From Heaven (2002), the film strips away the glossy veneer of affluent domestic life to expose the rot beneath. The claustrophobic apartment scenes and handheld camera work create an atmosphere of mounting anxiety that mirrors Tina's psychological state.

Frank Perry's direction avoids the melodramatic touches common to "women's pictures" of the era, instead adopting a semi-documentary style reminiscent of John Cassavetes. This approach would influence later feminist filmmakers like Barbara Loden with Wanda (1970) and Claudia Weill with Girlfriends (1978). The film's unflinching examination of female dissatisfaction and sexual politics helped pave the way for more explicit explorations in films like Looking for Mr. Goodbar (1977) and An Unmarried Woman (1978). SUBHEAD: Impact on 1970s Cinema and Beyond

movies.title: Three Women
movies.slug: Altman's dreamlike study of identity and female relationships in the American Southwest

sections.content: The film's influence can be traced through the wave of feminist-minded cinema that followed in the 1970s. Works like Alice Doesn't Live Here Anymore (1974) and Starting Over (1979) built on its honest portrayal of women's struggles for identity beyond traditional domestic roles. The raw authenticity of Snodgress's performance - which earned her an Oscar nomination - established a new template for depicting women's inner lives on screen, influencing performances from Gena Rowlands to Diane Keaton.
